# Workflow
To generate quantitative metabarcoding we are integrating multiple datastreams: 

- **metabarcoding of environmental DNA** samples using MiFish 12S primers, 
- metabarcoding from **mock communities** with known starting input concentrations using MiFish 12S primers,
-  and **qPCR of Coho salmon** (*Oncorhynchus kisutch*) 

[**Note**: qPCR was run on 3 other species Beluga (*Delphinapterus leucas*), Eulachon (*Thaleichthys pacificus*), and King salmon (*Oncorhynchus tshawytscha*).

Here we follow the workflow laid out in Andruszkiewicz Allan et al. 2023 [@allan2023quantifying].

![image](./Flowchart_gold_beluga_analysis_2.jpg)

# Data Organization & QA/QC 

As illustrated in Figure 2, there are a series of data organization and QA/QC steps needed to process the multiple data streams and files into a cohesive analysis. This section outlines the processes in more granular detail.

## Mock community data
- The raw and processed data has been published in Shelton et al. 2023 [@shelton2023toward] and Gold et al. 2023[@gold2023signal].

- Mock community metabarcoding data was processed using the Anacapa Toolkit pipeline following Gold et al. 2021 with an additional taxonomy fix step implemented for salmon (**Oncorhynchus sp.**) following Shelton et al. 2023.

- Data was post processed to remove poorly sequenced mock communities and confirm annotations to known input species following Shelton et al. 2023.

## Metabarcoding Environmental data

- Enviromental DNA Metabarcoding data was processed using the Anacapa Toolkit pipeline following Gold et al. 2021 [@gold2021improving] with an additional taxonomy fix step implemented for salmon (*Oncorhynchus* sp.) following Shelton et al. 2023. A total of five sequencing runs were conducted for this project, 3 runs from Kenai River samples and 2 runs from Twentymile River samples.

- Resulting amplicon sequence variant tables (ASVs) were then further processed using the Gruinard decontamination pipeline as implemented in [Gold et al. 2022](https://peerj.com/articles/14071/) [@gold2022manager]. Scripts to run the decontamination are in the decontam/ directories located within each of the five sequencing run directories.

- Metadata was organized and cleaned to allow for downstream sample merging.

- eDNA index was derived for all species following Kelly et al. 2019 [@kelly2019understanding]. This was done as high quality mock community data was only available for a distinct subset of taxa and this allowed for community analyses across a broader swath of observed taxa for supplemental analyses. 

#### Data

| File              | Description | Type | Path |
| ----- | ----------- | --- | ---- |
| `Anacapa_processed_` <br /> `sequence_data/`    |  Data processed from 5 sequencing runs (`Kenai_1`, `Kenai_2`, `Kenai_3`, `Twentymile_1`, `Twentymile_2`) using the Anacapa Toolkit as described in [Gold et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.13450).  | Data | `./data/eDNA_data/` <br /> `data/Anacapa_processed` <br /> `_sequence_data/` |
| `Raw_sequence_data`    |  Raw fastq reads   | Data | `./data/eDNA_data/` <br /> `data/Raw_sequence_data/` |


#### Code

| File              | Description | Type | Path |
| ----- | ----------- | --- | ---- |
| `Anacapa_scripts/`           | Directory of Anacapa QA/QC ASV generation & Anacapa classifier scripts run using using the `Global FishCard reference database` described in [Gold et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.13450)  | Code | `./data/eDNA_data/` <br /> `code/Anacapa_scripts/` |
| `taxonomy_fix/`           | Directory of scripts and data used to correct taxonomy. This approach is identical to that described for the mock community above. | Code & Data | `./data/eDNA_data/` <br /> `code/taxonomy_fix/scripts/` |
| `decontam/`    | These subdirectorties within each of the five sequencing run directories includes the code to run decontamination of each output Anacapa ASV table. Decontamination was completed with the following steps: 0) Retain only paired merged reads , 1)  Account for estimated rate tag jumping (index hopping) by subtracting proportional read abundances observed in positive controls from samples, 2) Retain PCR technical replicates with greater than 30K reads, 3) Retain ASVs with a probability of detection greater than the maximum estimated probability of an ASV being detected only once. This was implemented using a Site Occupancy Modeling framework on the pattern of presence of ASVs observed across the data set, 4) Discard Biological and PCR Technical replicates with greater than 99% dissimilarity from all other samples. | Data | `.data/eDNA_data/` <br /> `data/Anacapa_processed` <br /> `_sequence_data/` <br /> `[insert river]/` <br /> `[insert sequencing run]` <br /> `/decontam` |

## qPCR Data

- qPCR data was processed following Shelton et al. 2022 [@shelton2022environmental] using a bayesian model to estimate qPCR concentrations of environmental data from known standards.

- Metadata was organized and cleaned to allow for downstream sample merging.

#### Data

| ----- | ----------- | --- | ---- |
| `qPCR_raw/`    |  `Raw qPCR results from 10 distinct plates.` Eulachon, Coho, and Chinook were multiplexed together. Beluga was run separately. Each plate includes it's own standard curve with known concentrations as well as samples with unknown concentrations.  | Data | `.data/qPCR_results/` <br /> `data/qPCR_raw/` |
| `sample_metadata/`    |  Sample metadata from each of the 10 qPCR plates   | Data | `./data/qPCR_results/` <br /> `data/sample_metadata/` |

## Bias Corrected Metabarcoding
- Mock communities were used to calibrate eDNA metabarcoding results following Shelton et al. 2023. Here we focus on only the five common *Oncorhynchus* salmon species: Coho, King, Chum, Pink, and Sockeye. All five species had sufficient mock community data to accurately estimate amplification efficiencies.

## Estimating Abundance

### Metabarcoding Proportions x qPCR Absolute Abundance

- Proportional metabarcoding data for Coho was cross multiplied against qPCR absolute abundance concentrations to derive the total number of DNA molecules in a given sample following Andruszkiewicz Allan et al. 2023. Coho was chosen as the anchor species as it was the species amplified via qPCR that was the most commonly detected species across the metabarcoding data set. Estimates of quantitative abundance for the five species with bias corrected metabarcoding proportional data were then derived cross multiplying the observed proportional reads with the estimated total DNA molecules per sample.

## Analyses

Analyses conducted for the manuscript

### Main Manuscript

| File              | Description | Type | Path |
| ----- | ----------- | --- | ---- |
| `CIB_analysis_` <br /> `trimmed_` <br /> `20261109.Rmd` | Main Analysis Document  | Code | `analysis/scripts/` <br /> `CIB_analysis_` <br /> `trimmed_` <br /> `20261109.Rmd` |

- Beluga occurrence. Visual, qPCR, and metabarcoding detection rates for beluga were compared before, during, and after beluga river habitat use.

- Twentymile river quantitative metabarcoding time series. Estimated abundance of fish species from eDNA were compared before and during observations of Cook Inlet Beluga in Twentymile river.

- Summary of general statistics and diversity observed via eDNA metabarcoding data.

- General statistics and figures of fish species occurrences during periods of beluga observation on both Kenai and Twentymile River.

- Temporal and Spatial Variation. Specifically, an analysis of factors explaining variance in Kenai River environmental data, examining fish communities across time, site, and depth to inform future sampling strategies.

- Non-detections and the effects of swamping and rare molecules.
